notes:
Summary: Obsidian Sentinel is a mid-stage SaaS (customer KB + in-app support) exploring a hosted inference path for RAG. Primary needs: high QPS retrieval + cheap vector lookups, a low-latency reranker for top-k results, and predictable unit economics at scale.

Indexing/scale: currently ~8M canonical documents (20M+ dense chunks after shingling). Expected growth to 25-30M chunks in 6-9 months. They push daily delta updates (near-daily refresh) and want index warm/refresh to not block queries.

Performance targets: SLA for 95th pctl end-to-end search (retrieve + rerank) ~<150ms, engineering insists on <120ms for reranker component (90th pctl) to keep UX snappy. Target throughput 1k-2k QPS during peak.

Cost sensitivity: very cost-aware - target blended cost-per-query <= $0.01 at scale (including vector lookup + reranker costs). Will trade model size, quantization, and batching to hit this. Open to multi-tier routing: cheap approximate lookup to satisfy 80% queries, higher-cost exact/rerank for the rest.

Model preferences & routing: prefer open/quantized reranker models (instruction-tuned or small cross-encoders) with Redwood-managed fallbacks. Wants policy to route low-value queries to smaller cheaper models and escalate only when confidence is low. Also interested in embedding model A/B tests.

Security/compliance: SSO (SAML) a hard requirement, audit logs retention for 12 months for compliance, KMS integration, and EU data residency for a subset of customer data.

POC notes (shorthand/rep):
- "indexed 8M docs, shards configured, Faiss ivf tested; recall ok but tail latency high when reranker hits"
- "reranker sweep: 3 candidate models, best latency ~95ms median on Redwood hosted nodes, but cost projected high at 2k QPS"
- "prefetch/warm-cache idea: run nightly warms for top queries -> reduced cold-stall by ~40% in bench"
- "asked: can Redwood provide burst/buffer pricing or reserved capacity estimate?"

Timeline & stakeholders: AE Aisha (owner), SE Marco (tech lead), CSM Lina (handoff after close). Product lead: Jonah Krueger (internal contact), CTO: Nadine Ortiz. Decision window: Nov 2025.

Next steps (short):
- Run 72-hour soak at 1.5k QPS on hosted API (metrics: p95 latency, cost per successful query, error rate, index refresh time).
- Deliver two cost models: pure hosted at projected QPS and hybrid hosted->dedicated for high-volume routes.
- Complete security checkpoint: provide SOC2 excerpt and KMS integration doc.

Quotes/voice: "If we can't get predictable per-query economics at 2k QPS, we can't go forward".
